title: Custom software development
tagline: Software built around how your business actually works
summary: We design, build and modernize web and business applications for teams that have outgrown spreadsheets, off-the-shelf tools, or an ageing legacy system.
who: Operations, finance and product leaders at small and mid-sized businesses whose processes no longer fit a generic tool — or whose existing system is slow, fragile, and expensive to change.
problems: Manual, spreadsheet-driven workflows that don't scale and are error-prone
Off-the-shelf software that forces your team to work the wrong way
A legacy application that's slow, risky to change, and hard to hire for
Data trapped in disconnected tools with no single source of truth
deliverables: A working, documented application deployed to your cloud account
A clear data model and admin tooling your team can operate
Source-code handover and ownership terms defined in the agreement
Automated tests and a deployment pipeline, not just a one-off build
A phased modernization plan when replacing a legacy system
approach: Discovery: map the real workflow, constraints and success criteria
Architecture and a thin end-to-end slice to de-risk early
Short build iterations with working software you can review
Launch, then hand over code, docs and knowledge to your team
tech: Incremental migration from legacy stacks (Classic ASP, VB6, WinForms)
boundaries: We don't do big-bang rewrites that put your operations at risk — modernization is phased.
We scope a first milestone before quoting a full build, so you're not committing blind.
If an off-the-shelf tool genuinely fits better, we'll say so.

faqs.a: Source-code access, IP rights and handover requirements are agreed in writing before development starts.

faqs.q: Can you work with our existing system?
faqs.a: Usually yes — we commonly build alongside and incrementally replace a legacy system rather than forcing a rebuild.
Start with a conversation about goals, constraints and the existing system. We then propose an appropriate discovery phase or first milestone, including its scope and commercial terms.

title: Integrations & AI automation
tagline: Connect your tools and automate the manual work between them
summary: We connect the systems you already use — CRMs, accounting, payments, support, internal apps — and automate the repetitive work between them, including AI-assisted automation for tasks like document handling, triage and drafting.
who: Teams losing hours to copy-paste between tools, re-keying data, or chasing information across systems that don't talk to each other.
problems: The same data entered by hand into two or three different systems
Tools that don't integrate, creating silos and reconciliation work
Repetitive back-office tasks (sorting, tagging, drafting, routing) that eat staff time
No reliable, logged sync between your key systems
deliverables: Reliable integrations with authentication, retries and error logging
Automated workflows that remove specific manual steps
AI-assisted automations where they measurably save time (e.g. document extraction, classification, draft generation) — with a human review step
Monitoring and alerts so you know when something upstream breaks
approach: Map every system, data flow and manual step involved
Prioritize the automations with the clearest time saving
Build with secure auth, idempotency and full logging
Measure the time saved and tune from there
tech: REST and webhook integrations, message queues
Payments & finance: Stripe, PayPal, QuickBooks, Xero
CRM & support: Zoho, HubSpot, Salesforce, Twilio, SendGrid
AI automation: OpenAI and similar LLM APIs, document & vision pipelines
Health & device APIs where relevant to the project
boundaries: AI is used where it reliably helps — we don't add it for its own sake, and we keep a human in the loop for anything consequential.
We're honest about accuracy limits and build review/fallback steps into AI workflows.
We integrate with your approved tools and keep credentials server-side.

faqs.q: Is the AI reliable enough to trust?
faqs.a: For well-scoped tasks (extraction, classification, drafting) it saves real time, but we design workflows with validation and human review rather than full autonomy for anything that matters.

faqs.q: Will this break when a provider changes their API?
faqs.a: We build with error handling and monitoring so failures are caught and alerted, not discovered weeks later.

faqs.q: Can you automate just one painful process first?
faqs.a: Yes — that's usually the best way to start and prove the value before expanding.

title: Dedicated & hourly developers
tagline: The capacity you need. A way of working that fits.
summary: Extend your team with dedicated developers, or tackle a defined backlog with hourly development support. Discuss your stack, priorities and availability with us.
who: Founders and engineering leaders who need to move faster than hiring allows, or to add specific skills (mobile, DevOps, AI) for a defined period.
problems: Hiring the right senior engineer takes months you don't have
A roadmap that's slipping for want of capacity
A short-term need for a specific skill you don't want to hire full-time
Contractors who disappear or don't integrate with your team
deliverables: Developers matched to the technical needs and agreed scope
Work in your repositories, task board and review process
Progress updates and agreed reporting for hours and deliverables
An onboarding plan with access, communication and responsibilities defined
approach: Understand your stack, roadmap and the gap you're filling
Propose specific engineers with relevant experience
Onboard into your tools and ways of working
Work in your process with regular demos and reviews
tech: DevOps & cloud: AWS, Azure, CI/CD, containers
boundaries: Availability, working hours, time-zone overlap and notice periods are agreed in writing.
Hourly work is estimated and prioritised with you; rates and billing terms depend on scope.
Security, confidentiality, source-code rights and handover are covered in the agreement.

faqs.q: Dedicated developers or hourly support: which fits?
faqs.a: Dedicated development suits a sustained roadmap and ongoing collaboration. Hourly support suits a focused backlog or intermittent technical needs. Share the work and we can discuss the trade-offs.

faqs.q: Can we start with one developer?
faqs.a: Tell us the skills and time commitment you need. We will discuss a suitable arrangement and current availability before you commit.

faqs.q: How are hours and progress reported?
faqs.a: Agree a task backlog, estimates, reporting cadence and approval process before starting. Commercial terms and any minimum commitments are set out in the proposal.

faqs.q: Can you work with our time zone?
faqs.a: Share the collaboration hours your team needs. We agree workable overlap and communication expectations as part of scoping.

title: Zoho implementation & customization
tagline: Get real value from the Zoho tools you're paying for
summary: We implement, customize and integrate Zoho products — CRM, Creator, Books, People, Desk and Zoho One — so they fit your processes and connect to the rest of your systems.
who: Businesses that have bought into Zoho but aren't getting full value, or need custom apps, automations and integrations on top of it.
problems: A Zoho setup that doesn't match how your team actually works
Manual workflows that Zoho could automate
Zoho disconnected from your other tools and data
A need for custom apps or logic beyond the defaults
deliverables: Configured Zoho products mapped to your workflows
Custom modules, Deluge scripts and workflow automations
Integrations between Zoho and your other systems
Data migration and team enablement
approach: Assess current processes and where Zoho is underused
Design the configuration, automations and integrations
Implement, migrate data and connect third-party tools
Train your team and support the rollout
tech: Zoho CRM, Creator, Books, People, Desk, Inventory
boundaries: We'll tell you when a native Zoho feature already covers your need instead of building custom.
Integrations keep credentials secure and server-side.

faqs.q: Do you work across the whole Zoho suite?
faqs.a: Yes — from single products like CRM through to Zoho One and custom Creator apps and integrations.

faqs.q: Can you connect Zoho to our other tools?
faqs.a: Yes, that's one of the most common requests — accounting, payments, e-commerce and internal systems.

title: Growth & marketing engineering
tagline: Marketing automation and measurement for software businesses
summary: For product and SaaS teams, we set up the technical side of growth — analytics, attribution, email automation and landing pages — so marketing decisions are based on data, not guesses.
who: Software and SaaS companies that need marketing automation, reliable tracking and attribution wired up correctly.
problems: Marketing spend that can't be tied back to results
Email and lifecycle automation that was never set up properly
Analytics and attribution that can't be trusted
Landing pages and funnels that are slow to ship
deliverables: Analytics and conversion tracking implemented correctly
Email and lifecycle automation in your platform of choice
Fast, measurable landing pages
Reporting that connects activity to outcomes
approach: Audit the current stack, tracking and funnel
Fix measurement first so decisions are trustworthy
Build the automations and pages that matter most
Report on what's working and iterate
tech: Analytics: GA4, server-side tracking, consent handling
boundaries: We focus on the engineering and measurement side of growth, not vanity-metric campaigns.
We set up privacy-respecting, consent-aware tracking.

faqs.a: Our strength is the technical foundation — tracking, automation and pages. We can advise on campaigns but the measurement side is where we add the most value.

title: Mobile app development
tagline: Put your business in your customers’ hands.
summary: Design and build mobile applications for customers and field teams, with connected backends and clear, usable workflows.
who: Businesses building a customer app, a field-service tool or a mobile companion to an existing platform.
problems: Customers need a simpler way to access your service on a phone
Field teams need data capture and workflows away from a desk
An existing app needs better usability or integration
deliverables: User journeys and interface designs for the agreed platforms
Mobile application and backend/API integrations
Testing across the agreed devices and operating-system versions
Release preparation, documentation and a maintenance plan
approach: Understand users, workflows and platform constraints
Prototype the important journeys and agree a first release
Build, integrate and test on the agreed devices and environments
Plan deployment, documentation and ongoing maintenance
boundaries: Scope, delivery milestones, intellectual property and support are agreed in writing.
Third-party accounts, licences and platform fees are discussed during scoping.

faqs.q: Can one app support iOS and Android?
faqs.a: React Native and Flutter can share substantial code across platforms. Device integrations and user experience requirements determine whether a shared approach fits.
Offline support requires deliberate storage, synchronisation and conflict-handling design. Tell us where connectivity is unreliable so we can scope it properly.

faqs.q: Will you help with app store releases?
faqs.a: Release preparation can be included in the scope. Store accounts, review timelines and final approval remain subject to the platform’s requirements.

title: Desktop application development
tagline: Software that works where your business does.
summary: Build and modernise desktop applications for operational workflows, local data and existing business systems, with deployment planned around your environment.
who: Teams relying on Windows business software, established desktop tools or workflows that need access to local systems.
problems: A legacy application is becoming difficult to maintain
Local workflows and equipment do not fit a browser-only tool
Teams need a clear path from an old application to a supported platform
deliverables: Workflow and dependency assessment
Desktop interface and business logic for the agreed environment
Data migration and integration where included in scope
Installer, deployment guidance and handover documentation
approach: Understand users, workflows and platform constraints
Prototype the important journeys and agree a first release
Build, integrate and test on the agreed devices and environments
Plan deployment, documentation and ongoing maintenance
tech: Legacy VB6 and Classic ASP assessment
boundaries: Scope, delivery milestones, intellectual property and support are agreed in writing.
Third-party accounts, licences and platform fees are discussed during scoping.

faqs.q: Can you modernise our existing Windows application?
faqs.a: Start with the source code, dependencies and deployment environment. We can assess what should be retained, replaced or connected to newer services.

faqs.q: Do you support every desktop operating system?
faqs.a: Our existing stack includes Windows and .NET. Share any macOS or Linux requirements so compatibility and the implementation approach can be assessed before a proposal.

faqs.q: How do we avoid disrupting daily operations?
faqs.a: Plan migration around representative data, acceptance testing, staged deployment and a rollback path. The appropriate approach depends on the current system.
